domain_guidance.summary: This domain evaluates reading comprehension and the ability to analyze written text. It accounts for 26.0 percent of the exam content and requires candidates to demonstrate strong analytical skills to interpret various passages effectively.

This domain covers mathematical concepts including fractions, decimals, percentages, and algebra. It represents 23.0 percent of the total exam weight and tests your ability to solve complex numerical problems accurately within the testing environment.

This domain focuses on scientific principles and knowledge, making up 29.0 percent of the exam. It is the largest section of the test and requires a deep understanding of biological and physical sciences to succeed.

This domain assesses English and language usage skills, accounting for 22.0 percent of the exam content. Candidates must demonstrate proficiency in grammar, sentence structure, and vocabulary to succeed in this section of the test.

editorial.exam_day_guidance: Arrive prepared to manage your time across the 170 questions. Ensure you are familiar with the 209-minute duration. Use the provided scratch paper or tools if permitted, and pace yourself to address all four content areas within the allotted time.

faq.answer_text: The passing score for the exam is determined by individual nursing programs. You should check with your specific institution or ATI TEAS to understand the requirements for your application and ensure you meet the necessary standards.

The total duration for the exam is 209 minutes. Candidates must complete all questions within this time limit, so effective time management is required for a successful testing experience during the official exam session.

For information regarding the current certification path or any updates to the exam, please check with ATI TEAS directly to ensure you have the most accurate and up-to-date information for your specific nursing program application.

editorial.overview: The TEAS Nursing Entrance Exam is administered by ATI TEAS to assess academic readiness for nursing programs. The exam covers four distinct domains: reading, math, science, and English and language usage. It consists of 170 total questions and is completed within a duration of 209 minutes. This assessment serves as a standard measure for applicants seeking entry into nursing education programs globally, providing schools with a consistent metric to evaluate the academic potential of prospective students across various health-related disciplines.
editorial.preparation_strategy: Review the official study manual and practice assessments to understand the exam format. Focus on the four content areas by practicing fractions, decimals, percentages, and algebraic equations. Use the provided distance, area, and volume formulas to build proficiency. Consult the official ATI TEAS resources to identify specific topics for each domain and ensure you are familiar with the question types and time constraints to perform well.
editorial.who_should_take: This exam is for individuals applying to nursing programs who must demonstrate academic proficiency. It is appropriate for students preparing for health profession careers who need to meet specific entrance requirements set by their chosen nursing schools for admission.
